guards.what: N1: `while (base.Owner.HasOpenPotionSlots)` with a `break` on procure failure (DelicateFrond.cs:15-22) vs `while player.has_open_potion_slot` with no break (delicate_frond.py:24-25)
guards.rationale: Checked deliberately because a missing break is a hang risk, and it is not one here: PlayerCombatState.add_potion (player.py:116-121) can only return False when `None not in self.potions`, which is the negation of the loop condition has_open_potion_slot (player.py:146-149), so the loop always terminates. The one C# failure mode that is NOT belt-full -- the Sozu veto -- is guard G2's subject, and there the sim does not merely fail to break, it succeeds. HasOpenPotionSlots itself matches: `_potionSlots.Any(p => p == null)` vs `None in self.potions`, so empty slots and a nulled slot mean the same thing on both sides (the belt is never compacted -- player.py:123-127).
